$comment: Per-package prose that a manifest cannot carry, merged into each package's README by scripts/gen-package-docs.mjs. Keep this file the only hand-written source: editing a generated README is overwritten by the next `npm run package-docs`, and `package-docs:check` will say so. `role` decides whether the page opens as a product or as an internal dependency; `audience` answers 'should I be installing this?'; `fits` is where it sits in the composition. See docs/packages.md for the same map in one place.

roles.host-plugin: Host plugin — runs beside the agent in the DSH process
roles.browser-half: Browser half — runs in the workspace UI
roles.shared: Shared contract — depended on by both halves

@deepwatch/cli.audience: Anyone who wants the whole DeepWatch workspace and does not already run a DeepSeek Harness. This is the package behind the `deepwatch` command.
@deepwatch/cli.prerequisites: Node ≥ 22.19. Python 3.11–3.13 with `watch-skill` installed for the perception and verification half; `deepwatch doctor` reports what is missing and `deepwatch setup` offers to fetch what it can.

example.caption: Set up once, then serve a workspace:
example.code:
npm install -g @deepwatch/cli
deepwatch doctor              # what is installed, what is missing
deepwatch setup               # build the runtime, compose the profile
deepwatch web --workspace ./my-project

@deepwatch/cli.fits: It composes `@deepwatch/dsh-bundle` into a DeepSeek Harness profile, manages the runtime that profile needs, and serves it. Everything it installs is one of the other nineteen packages.

@deepwatch/dsh-bundle.audience: Anyone already running a DeepSeek Harness who wants to add Watch to it without moving to a different product.
@deepwatch/dsh-bundle.prerequisites: A DSH installation at the pinned baseline, and `watch-skill` on `PATH` for anything that needs Core.
@deepwatch/dsh-bundle.fits: The single package a profile names. It declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` reconciles thirteen Watch packages into the profile's layer stack in one step.

@deepwatch/dsh-core-bridge.audience: Composed by the bundle. Install it directly only to speak to Watch Core from a host of your own.
@deepwatch/dsh-core-bridge.prerequisites: `watch-skill` reachable on `PATH`, or an explicit `command`. Without one the Bridge reports `core_missing` and leaves the workspace usable with Watch features disabled — it does not fall back to a mock.
@deepwatch/dsh-core-bridge.fits: The only thing that talks to Watch Core. Every other package reaches Core through it, which is what makes Core the sole source of a verdict.

@deepwatch/dsh-tools.audience: Composed by the bundle. This is where Watch's capabilities become agent tools.
@deepwatch/dsh-tools.fits: Registers the 22 `watch_*` tools an agent is offered, and turns each tool call into a receipt. It records what a call did; it never decides whether the work was correct.

@deepwatch/dsh-memory.audience: Composed by the bundle. Off unless a profile turns it on.
@deepwatch/dsh-memory.prerequisites: A writable directory for the ledger. The store is plaintext; it is created owner-only where the operating system enforces file modes, and there is no encryption at rest in this release.
@deepwatch/dsh-memory.fits: An append-only event ledger under the workspace boundary. `@deepwatch/dsh-wiki` projects it into pages and `@deepwatch/dsh-client-memory` presents it.

@deepwatch/dsh-library.prerequisites: A Bridge connected to Core, and `libraryRoots` naming the directories the index may read — empty by default, so a deployment that has not said where its evidence lives gets a tool reporting nothing to search rather than one guessing.
@deepwatch/dsh-library.fits: The catalogue behind the Library screen: sources, revisions, index state, search, facets and collections.

@deepwatch/dsh-live.audience: Composed by the bundle. Needed for live and browser sessions.
@deepwatch/dsh-live.prerequisites: Core built with the `[loop]` extra, and a browser installed by `playwright install chromium`, for anything that drives a page.
@deepwatch/dsh-live.fits: One clock across streams, with cursors, declared gaps, a bounded buffer and a reconnect policy — so "what was on screen when that was said" has an answer rather than a guess.

@deepwatch/dsh-technology.prerequisites: DSH Models and Providers configured in the host profile.
@deepwatch/dsh-technology.fits: Where "this model can see images" is recorded, and where a capability is bound to a role. The Settings surface reads it; nothing else guesses at a model's abilities.

@deepwatch/dsh-trajectory.fits: Puts Watch records inside the Harness Trajectory, so a receipt, a verdict and the turn that produced them share one selection, one deep link and one replay.

@deepwatch/dsh-wiki.prerequisites: `@deepwatch/dsh-memory` mounted, since the ledger is what it projects.
@deepwatch/dsh-wiki.fits: Deterministic projections over the memory ledger: the same ledger produces the same pages, so a wiki page is a view and never a second copy of the truth.

@deepwatch/dsh-tenancy.audience: Composed by the bundle. Relevant to a shared or multi-user deployment.
@deepwatch/dsh-tenancy.fits: Tenants, roles, remote workers, sharing and audit — decided server-side. A browser half may render a permission; it may not grant one.

@deepwatch/dsh-workspace.audience: Composed by the bundle and loaded by the DSH client loader.
@deepwatch/dsh-workspace.fits: The product shell: modes, header, inspector and the sensory timeline every other surface mounts into.

@deepwatch/dsh-client-evidence.audience: Composed by the bundle and loaded by the DSH client loader.
@deepwatch/dsh-client-evidence.fits: How a verdict looks: the result card, the check list, the contract digest, and Compare for two runs of the same contract. It presents what Core decided and decides nothing itself.

@deepwatch/dsh-client-memory.audience: Composed by the bundle and loaded by the DSH client loader.
@deepwatch/dsh-client-memory.fits: The Memory surfaces — taste, timeline, wiki, decisions, lessons, failures and sources — over the ledger `@deepwatch/dsh-memory` keeps.

@deepwatch/dsh-client-settings.audience: Composed by the bundle and loaded by the DSH client loader.
@deepwatch/dsh-client-settings.fits: The Technology & Capability Center: role bindings, engines, sources, memory, verification and diagnostics. This is the screen that says what is ready and what is missing.

@deepwatch/dsh-client-remotes.audience: Composed by the bundle and loaded by the DSH client loader.
@deepwatch/dsh-client-remotes.fits: Mounts Watch's generated Typert Remote into `ctx.remote`, so every client call reaches the host through one generated, type-checked surface instead of hand-written fetches.

@deepwatch/dsh-client-brand.audience: Composed by the bundle. Install it directly to build a surface that matches Watch's identity.
@deepwatch/dsh-client-brand.fits: The product identity and the semantic status tokens every other surface reads, plus the attribution and independence statements the product renders.

@deepwatch/dsh-contracts.audience: Anyone implementing either side of the Bridge — a host plugin, a browser half, or a client of your own.
@deepwatch/dsh-contracts.prerequisites: None. Types and schemas only; it pulls in nothing at runtime.
@deepwatch/dsh-contracts.fits: The wire shapes both halves agree on. Changing a shape here changes both sides at once, which is the reason it is a package rather than two copies.

@deepwatch/dsh-sdk.audience: Third parties building a Watch capability of their own.
@deepwatch/dsh-sdk.prerequisites: A DSH host to mount into.

example.caption: The four verbs a capability gets:
example.code: import { declare, probe, observe, request } from '@deepwatch/dsh-sdk'

@deepwatch/dsh-sdk.fits: The supported extension path: declare a capability, probe whether its prerequisites hold, observe what happens, request work. It is how a capability joins the composition without patching it.

@deepwatch/dsh-adapters.audience: Anyone exporting Watch's memory into another tool. Nothing depends on it.

example.caption: Export the wiki as an Obsidian vault:
example.code:
import { buildWiki, toVault } from '@deepwatch/dsh-adapters'

const vault = toVault(buildWiki(records), { name: 'Watch' })

@deepwatch/dsh-adapters.fits: Obsidian vaults and LLMWiki bundles, generated from the ledger. An edit in an exported vault is a proposal, never a change: Watch is the record and the folder is a copy.
